# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** 76 years old (prior to his death)  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c16 P15](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Keeper of the Four Winds Lighthouse; former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>; Jim Boyd  <sub>[v4 c22 P17](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0017), [v4 c24 P11](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0011)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim was a tall, ungainly, and stooped man who possessed great strength and endurance. He had a homely, deeply lined, and bronzed face with spare jaws, a rugged mouth, a square brow, and a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders. His remarkably blue, deep-set eyes often twinkled or looked out seaward with a wistful, searching gaze. In his final spring, he appeared noticeably frailer, stooped, and grayer.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 c30 P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 c30 P11](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0011)_

## Personality

Captain Jim was a high-souled, simple-minded, and true-hearted man with a youthful spirit and an easygoing, placid disposition. He was a passionate worshipper of beauty and possessed an incurable habit of being cheerful and enjoying life, even through hardships. Deeply hospitable and kind, he believed in meddling whenever it served a good cause. He was also a master storyteller who possessed a rare, wise, and refreshing nature.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c9 P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018), [v4 c34 P23](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0023)_

## History

Captain Jim grew up on Prince Edward Island, developing a passion for the sea inherited from his mother's side of the family. At sixteen, he formed a deep friendship with the Glen schoolmaster, John Selwyn, before running off to sea to spend five decades sailing to every corner of the globe. In his youth, he suffered a profound tragedy when his sweetheart, Margaret, died after drifting out to sea in a storm. He remained a bachelor for the rest of his life. After retiring from the sea, he became the keeper of the Four Winds Lighthouse. He rescued a injured, amnesiac Dick Moore in a Havana boarding house and brought him back to his wife Leslie. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to Four Winds, Captain Jim quickly became one of their closest friends and a constant guest at their home. He shared his life-book of written memories with writer Owen Ford, collaborating with him to get his travels and life story published. Before his death, he rejoiced in the birth of Gilbert and Anne's son Little Jem, who was named in his honor. Following his death, his collection of world curiosities was bequeathed to Little Jem.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P9](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0009), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c28 P35](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0035), [v4 c34 P18](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0018), [v4 c34 P23](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0023), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028), [v5 c2 P69](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0069), [v5 c6 P29](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0029)_

## Background by volume

- Came from a family of sea-going relatives on his mother's side  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- Fell asleep in the garden as an eight-year-old child and found comfort in the moon  <sub>[v4 c7 P63](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0063)</sub>
- Befriended schoolmaster John Selwyn at the age of sixteen  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- Ran off to sea as a young man and spent most of his life sailing worldwide  <sub>[v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- Lost his early love, Margaret, when her boat drifted out to sea during a storm  <sub>[v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c35 P35](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0035)</sub>
- Sailed on the Gray Gull with his old crony Henry Pollack  <sub>[v4 c24 P11](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0011)</sub>
- Rescued an injured Dick Moore in Havana and brought him back home  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>
- Saved an abandoned cat named the First Mate  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>
- Collected curiosities from all over the world  <sub>[v5 c2 P69](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0069), [v5 c6 P29](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0029)</sub>
- Had no children of his own  <sub>[v4 c34 P18](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0018)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m right down pleased to meet you, Mistress Blythe; and I hope you’ll be as happy as the first bride was who came here. I can’t wish you no better than THAT.  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

> You’re young and I’m old, but our souls are about the same age, I reckon. We both belong to the race that knows Joseph, as Cornelia Bryant would say.  <sub>[v4 c7 P54](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0054)</sub>

> I saved his life, and when you’ve saved a creature’s life you’re bound to love it. It’s next thing to giving life.  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>

> I’ve kind of contracted a habit of enj’ying things. It’s got so chronic that I believe I even enj’y the disagreeable things. It’s great fun thinking they can’t last.  <sub>[v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)</sub>

> I don’t think I’m a coward, Mistress Blythe—I’ve looked an ugly death in the face more than once without blenching. But the thought of a lingering death does give me a queer, sick feeling of horror.  <sub>[v4 c35 P36](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0036)</sub>
